title: Leftist Professor Doxxes ICE Agent, Urges Crowd To ‘F*ck Him Up’
text:
(Photo by Rich Fury/Getty Images)

University professor Melina Abdullah doxxed an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agent before inviting a crowd to “f*ck him up” during a Sunday event.

Abdullah — who teaches at the California State University, Los Angeles — spoke at an event described on its invitation as a “summit to end the terror against the people,” where participants learn how to challenge the Trump administration’s “intensified assault on civil liberties against immigrant communities.” (RELATED: City Council Votes To Allow Non-Citizens To Serve As Police Officers)

“The killer ICE agent, who we got on good authority, is right down the road at the Hilton Garden Inn in Oxnard,” Abdullah said, offering to show the crowd a “picture of his pig ass.”

The agent, Brian Palacios, shot and killed Keith Porter Jr. while off duty on New Year’s Eve 2025. Porter was firing a rifle in the air in celebration when Palacios confronted him, and then allegedly pointed and fired at Porter before being fatally shot. Palacios has not been charged with a crime.

🚨🚨🚨 Why is @CalStateLA professor Melina Abdullah identifying a specific ICE agent, telling a crowd where he may be staying, giving the street address, and repeatedly saying to “fuck him up”?“Brian Palacios may be staying at the Hilton Garden Inn at 2000 Solar Drive… fuck… pic.twitter.com/k4eijHhZ7n

“You see the devil right there, fuck him up,” Abdullah said before giving the address of the inn. “So fuck him up. fuck him up. I’m sorry, I’m already on the motherfucking list.”

Abdullah, who was wearing a “Black Lives Matter” shirt, then invited the audience to read the 1972 book “Blood in My Eye” by George Jackson — a black radical who was imprisoned for armed robbery, linked to the murders of four prison guards and two inmates, and was killed trying to escape prison. In the book, Jackson writes that the “government of the U.S.A. and all that it stands for, all that it represents, must be destroyed” and calls for revolutionaries to begin “numbering, naming, compiling information” on the regime’s “secret police.”

Continuing her screed, Abdullah urged her listeners to “use every single tool in your toolbox.”

“Whether it be powerful-ass. prayer like Mama Harriet Tubman, whether it be standing on front lines and putting your body on the line like it’s necessary in this moment, whether it be giving a dollar — all of those tools are absolutely necessary,” she said. “So when I say fuck him up, and I say fuck Brian Palacios up, who may be staying at the Hilton Garden Inn, when I say fuck him up, I mean in many ways.”

Civic leader and co-founder of the Black Lives Matter Los Angeles chapter, Melina Abdullah, poses for a photo after voting at the Staples Center early on November 3, 2020, in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by VALERIE MACON/AFP via Getty Images)

“They don’t get to do their s*ht invisibly. They don’t get to do their dirt in the dark. Shine a light on they motherfucking ass,” Abdullah continued. “There should be nowhere that they go where they are comfortable.”

Abdullah is described by the university as a “recognized expert on race, gender, class, and social movements” and a “womanist scholar-activist” who links the academy to the “broader struggles for the liberation of oppressed people.”

Speakers at the event also included a member of the Party for Socialism and Liberation, a member of which was charged in August 2025 for allegedly shooting two Israeli Embassy staffers before yelling “Free Free Palestine.”

ICE agents have faced heavy amounts of doxxing as tensions between protestors and law enforcement continue.

Cal State LA told the Daily Caller that it is aware of the statements made by Abdullah but noted that she was speaking at “an off-campus event that was not sponsored by, affiliated with, or authorized by” the university, adding that the professor was attending in an “individual capacity, not representing the university.”

“The university respects free speech, including speech with which the university strongly disagrees. The CSU and Cal State LA do not agree with or condone hatred, threats, or violence of any kind,” the university added. “Cal State LA remains fully committed to fostering a safe, inclusive, and respectful learning and working environment for all members of the Golden Eagle community.”
